questions.question: What is Ruby's exception hierarchy?
questions.title: Ruby's Exception Hierarchy
questions.direct_answer: All exceptions descend from Exception. Under it: StandardError (the normal app errors you rescue — RuntimeError, ArgumentError, NoMethodError, TypeError) and other branches (SystemExit for exit, SignalException for signals, NoMemoryError). The rule: rescue StandardError or below; don't rescue Exception (it catches SystemExit and signals). A bare rescue catches StandardError (the default), which is most app errors. When you define a custom exception, inherit from StandardError (or a specific one like StandardError) so it's caught by the default rescue. Knowing the hierarchy tells you what a rescue will and won't catch.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know Exception is the root, StandardError is the app-error branch (rescue this), and bare rescue catches StandardError.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Rescuing Exception (catches SystemExit/signals), or not knowing bare rescue catches StandardError (not Exception).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Exception is the root; StandardError is the app-error branch (RuntimeError, ArgumentError). rescue catches StandardError by default; don't rescue Exception (catches signals).

sections.content:
Exception is the root; StandardError is the branch you rescue; don't rescue Exception.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  E[Exception] --> SE[StandardError -> rescue this]
  E --> SY[SystemExit -> don't rescue]
  E --> SI[SignalException -> don't rescue]
  SE --> R[RuntimeError]
  SE --> A[ArgumentError]
  SE --> N[NoMethodError]
```

sections.title: The hierarchy
sections.content:
```ruby
# The key branches:
#   Exception                      <- DON'T rescue this
#     StandardError                <- rescue this (or below)
#       RuntimeError               <- raise with no class -> RuntimeError
#       ArgumentError              <- wrong number/type of args
#       NoMethodError              <- calling a missing method
#       TypeError, NameError, ...
#     SystemExit                   <- exit() raises this
#     SignalException              <- Ctrl-C
#     NoMemoryError

# Bare rescue catches StandardError (the default):
begin
  risky
rescue => e            # catches StandardError (RuntimeError, etc.)
  puts e.class            # RuntimeError
end

# rescue Exception catches EVERYTHING (including exit) — avoid:
begin
  exit                    # raises SystemExit
rescue Exception => e    # would catch SystemExit! DON'T
  puts 'swallowed exit'
end
```
